report.summary: Chunk 5 of 6: __init__ continues, run() method with storage check, intent recording, worktree creation, admin dir pointer reading, runner execution, artifact capture, gate execution, and branch reaping.
risks: _reap | high | reap_branches() called but manager's implementation not shown; if it deletes branches outside this process's allocation, could remove real work. | Verify manager.reap_branches() only deletes branches allocated in this process.

_run_with_ledger | high | self._admin_dir is read from worktree pointer but not used in this chunk; if _git commands later do not use it, the pointer is irrelevant and the security measure is ineffective. | Check that _git methods use self._admin_dir as git_dir.

run | medium | require_storage checks _existing_ancestor(worktree_root) but worktree_root may not exist yet; if it fails, attempt returns STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE without creating worktree. | Confirm that _existing_ancestor handles non-existent root gracefully.

_run_with_ledger | medium | persist_to_store returns a locator summary but artifact_path and artifact_locator are set only if locator is not None; if persist_error occurs, error may be overwritten by later checks. | Ensure error handling covers all branches.

_run_with_ledger | low | The comment about 'THIS LINE WAS self._admin_dir = None' suggests a historical bug; the line now reads self._admin_dir = _read_gitdir_pointer(worktree) which is correct per the comment. | No action needed.
todos: Verify that _git commands in this module use self._admin_dir as the git directory.
Confirm that reap_branches() in GitWorktreeManager is safe against deleting branches not allocated by this process.
Ensure that _existing_ancestor() works correctly when worktree_root does not exist yet.

handoff.purpose: Complete __init__ and implement run() method with full lifecycle: storage check, ledger, worktree, runner, artifact, gates, and reaping.

symbols.name: Attempt.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes instance attributes including _gate, _manager, _reap_enabled, _artifact_dir, _ledger, _ledger_path, _owns_ledger, branch, effect_key, _admin_dir.

symbols.name: Attempt.run
symbols.note: Entry point for attempting a task. Checks storage, resolves base revision, gets ledger, calls _run_with_ledger, then reaps branch. Returns AttemptResult.

symbols.name: Attempt._reap
symbols.note: Deletes this attempt's branch via manager.reap_branches() if _reap_enabled is True. Returns result with optional reap_error or reaped report.

symbols.name: Attempt._run_with_ledger
symbols.note: Records intent, creates worktree, runs runner, captures patch, persists artifact, runs gates, and resolves intent.

claims.text: The returned artifact is data. Applying it to the primary checkout is a separate, human-invoked act that this module intentionally does not provide.
claims.why: The method returns AttemptResult which contains the artifact data; no code in this chunk applies it to any checkout.

claims.text: Resolving the base is a READ of the primary checkout, not an effect, so it happens before the intent -- the payload can then name the exact revision the candidate was built on.
claims.why: The code calls _resolve_base() before any ledger.record_intent() call, and the resolved base_revision is included in the payload.

claims.text: No durable record is possible, so no effect may be performed.
claims.why: If _get_ledger() raises, the method returns STATE_WORKTREE_FAILED without proceeding to record_intent or worktree creation.

claims.text: gates on an unmodified tree would pass without judging anything; that vacuous green is exactly what must not be reported as `clean`.
claims.why: When artifact.is_empty, state is set to STATE_NO_CHANGE and error is set, bypassing gate execution.

claims.text: A reap that could not run is REPORTED on the result instead, so a silently growing ref namespace stays observable.
claims.why: If reap_branches() raises, the exception is caught and stored as reap_error in the result via _replace.

claims.text: The decision itself is entirely the manager's, and deliberately so: it deletes only branches THIS manager allocated in THIS process, whose worktree has been through cleanup, and whose tip still matches the sha it read at allocation.
claims.why: The implementation of reap_branches() is not in this chunk; we cannot verify these constraints.

claims.text: Passing `keep_worktree=True` therefore reaps nothing, because the cleanup precondition never becomes true.
claims.why: The relationship between keep_worktree and cleanup precondition is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: READ THE ADMIN POINTER NOW, WHILE NO CANDIDATE CODE HAS RUN.
claims.why: self._admin_dir is set immediately after worktree creation, before any runner code executes (runner is called later in the try block).

claims.text: Reading it here and passing --git-dir explicitly afterwards is what makes the pointer irrelevant.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain any _git calls that use self._admin_dir; the claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: THIS LINE WAS `self._admin_dir = None` AND THE COMMENT ABOVE STAYED. That is the whole vector: every test that calls `_git` directly went on passing, because they supply `git_dir=` themselves, and only the one test that goes through `run()` could see it.
claims.why: The current code has `self._admin_dir = _read_gitdir_pointer(worktree)`, not `None`. The comment describes a historical bug that is now fixed.

claims.text: A guard that is built and not connected is indistinguishable from a guard, right up until it is measured through the product.
claims.why: The comment is a general observation; the code now connects the guard by reading the pointer.

observations.what: self._admin_dir is read from worktree pointer but never used in this chunk; subsequent _git calls may not use it.
The _reap method calls self._manager.reap_branches() which could potentially delete branches not allocated by this process if not implemented safely.
require_storage checks _existing_ancestor(self._manager.worktree_root) but worktree_root may not exist yet; if it fails, attempt returns STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE without creating worktree.
The persist_to_store method returns a locator summary but artifact_path and artifact_locator are only set if locator is not None; if persist_error occurs, error may be overwritten by later checks.
The comment about the historical bug (self._admin_dir = None) is now outdated; the code correctly reads the pointer.
